2026-08-14 — PARTIALLY NARROWED, not closed. The premise 'zero analytics' was too strong: Render's own HTTP request logs already record path + user-agent for every hit, so the CRAWL half of this question was answerable all along with no instrumentation, no client script, and no consent surface. Built `scripts/crawl-read.mjs` (reads the Render logs API, aggregates by crawler; `--selfcheck` covers the UA-classification and label-parsing logic) and ran a 7-day read. Findings: (1) ZERO Google hits of any kind in 7 days — not Googlebot, not Google-Extended. Google does not appear to know this site exists, which means the bottleneck is discovery-by-Google, and no amount of additional SEO surface fixes that; the GSC property is the unblock and it is now evidence-backed rather than speculative. (2) There IS a live discovery channel already working: GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot poll /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml on a DAILY cadence (~15:2x UTC, unbroken 8/07-8/13), and GPTBot ran a full content crawl on 2026-08-12 17:43 covering /, /about, /methods, /colophon, /poster, /embed/docs. This is the first real evidence this project has ever had about who wants it, and it vindicates the llms.txt + .md-mirror strategy. (3) That GPTBot content crawl PREDATES the Phase 12 ship by a day, so it saw none of the 8 new routes; GPTBot has since re-fetched the sitemap (8/13 15:32Z) which now lists them. No crawler has fetched a /cycles* page yet. What crawl logs still CANNOT answer: impressions, queries, ranking position, or whether an indexed page was ever shown to a human. Those still need GSC, so the close condition below is unchanged.

2026-08-15 — THE PHASE 12 ROUTES ARE BEING CRAWLED. Read 6 days early because the 8/15 P2 continuity pass ran the instrument rather than waiting for the 08-21 date; the gate was already readable. `node scripts/crawl-read.mjs --days 7` at 2026-08-15T15:2xZ: GPTBot ran a full content crawl at 2026-08-15T10:27:04Z-10:27:38Z covering / , /cycles, ALL EIGHT /cycles/<slug> routes (kondratiev, schlesinger-jr, strauss-howe, perez, dalio, turchin, khaldun, huntington) AND all eight ?focus=<id> deep links, then returned at 10:54Z for RSC navigation payloads (/?_rsc=...&focus=perez, /cycles?_rsc=...) — i.e. it was traversing the app's client routing, not just fetching static URLs. This ANSWERS question (a) of the old 08-21 read with a YES and closes it. Derived latency, useful for future ships: the sitemap first listed the 8 routes on 2026-08-13 15:32Z (GPTBot's own re-fetch) and the content crawl landed 2026-08-15 10:27Z — approximately 43 hours, across two intervening daily sitemap polls (8/14 15:37Z, 8/15 10:27Z). So a new route on this site is LLM-crawled in about two days, and the internal-linking worry in the old branching was unfounded — no action needed there. This is the first evidence this project has ever had that a discovery channel is actually delivering to its newest surface.

Still open and UNCHANGED: Google is at ZERO for the 7-day window — no Googlebot, no Google-Extended, no Google-other. Positive control for that zero (per the number-provenance floor): the same classifier recorded 67 GPTBot + 9 OAI-SearchBot + 1 other-bot hits in the same window, the classified buckets sum exactly to the 2401 raw log lines, and `--selfcheck` unit-asserts the Googlebot and Google-Extended branches specifically — so a Google hit would have been recorded had one occurred. The zero is measured, not a dead probe.

CAUTION on the non-crawler buckets — do NOT report these as humans. The same read shows 1481 'browser-ish' and 778 'unknown (no UA)' lines (~323/day). 'browser-ish' is a UA-SHAPE fallback bucket (anything that is not a known crawler, not empty, and not our own tooling), and the number-provenance floor requires that crawler/human attribution verify official IP ranges rather than UA strings alone. On a site with zero Google presence and no inbound links, ~323/day of browser-shaped traffic is far more likely to be scanners and scrapers with spoofed UAs than readers. Treat the human-residual question as OPEN and unanswered; answering it needs reverse-DNS / IP-range verification, which is a bigger change than reporting the existing bucket.

2026-08-18 — RE-SEQUENCED by the citability research + domain purchase. (1) The two-engine citability research (skylark-site research-library 2026-08-18-sinusoidal-cycles-citability.md) confirmed GSC verification as the #1 evidence-backed config action — Google indexing is a categorical prerequisite for AI Overviews — and simultaneously RETIRED GPTBot crawl depth as a KPI (training-only traffic, ~1,700 crawls per referral; the new proxy hierarchy is utm_source=chatgpt.com referrals > ChatGPT-User > OAI-SearchBot). The GSC property should therefore be created on the NEW domain AFTER the cutover, not on the skylarkcreations.com subdomain — verifying the old host first would mean verifying twice. 2026-08-20 — THE UNBLOCK LANDED. Domain cutover shipped (commit d36770b): sinusoidalhistory.com is canonical; the legacy subdomain, the .org twin, and both www variants issue permanent redirects with paths preserved (verified live end-to-end, including /cycles/turchin and the frozen /data/state-2026.csv). What remains is purely a WAIT: Google needs time to crawl a domain it has never seen. TWO reads, deliberately staged. (a) SOON — 2026-08-22: did the PROVEN channel survive the host change? GPTBot/OAI-SearchBot polled robots.txt + sitemap.xml daily on the old subdomain; the question is whether they follow the 308 onto sinusoidalhistory.com and resume the daily cadence there. If that goes silent, the cutover broke the one discovery channel that was actually working and it is urgent, not a wait. (b) LATER — 2026-09-03: the Google question. GSC was verified 2026-08-20, so a zero before a fresh 14-day window from that date means nothing; do not read it as the cutover failing.

2026-08-21 — BOTH STAGED QUESTIONS ANSWERED EARLY, AND THE BIG ONE FLIPPED: GOOGLE ARRIVED. Ran the 14-day read one day ahead of the 8/22 date because two post-cutover daily-poll windows had already passed (same early-read precedent as 8/15). Findings, in severity order. (1) The 'Google at zero' era is OVER: 731 Google-family hits in the window (188 Googlebot + 543 Google-other), ALL post-cutover — Googlebot fetched sitemap.xml 2026-08-20 22:18Z, hours after David submitted it through the new GSC property, then polled robots.txt near-hourly overnight and content-crawled /cycles/<slug> routes, /data/spectral/*.svg, and the paired CSVs through 8/21 17:08Z. Google-other (likely GoogleOther/InspectionTool onboarding the new domain) swept every page including all 10 cycle routes, /llms.txt, and /about.md. (2) Read (a) answered YES: the LLM channel survived the host change — OAI-SearchBot observed following the old-host 308 to a 200 on the new host in the same second (8 hits in the trailing 24h), and GPTBot crawled in-window: 13 sitemap fetches, all 10 cycle routes, all spectral SVGs + verdicts.json, the v1 API, and the frozen state-2026.csv (200 hits/14d; 2 in the trailing 24h). The channel-break escalation branch is dead. (3) Provenance: complete=true, buckets sum (11,883 lines), snapshot appended to docs/crawl-reads.jsonl. 2026-09-08 — THE CRAWL LEG OF THE 09-03 GATE IS ANSWERED (5 days late; the project had no session between 08-30 and 09-08, so the gate simply went unread — nothing blocked it). This was also the FIRST time this row's readCommand ever executed through the gate: the first attempt was killed at the 60s default cap, because a 14-day read paginates ~250 pages against Render's 30 req/min logs API and crawl-read.mjs backs off on 429 by design, so the backoff waits ARE the runtime. Raised readCommandTimeoutMs to the 600000ms cap; the re-run took 548s, exit 0, complete=true, 25,215 log lines, snapshot #3 appended to docs/crawl-reads.jsonl. Findings, in severity order. (1) GOOGLE HELD AND DEEPENED. Googlebot 375 hits/14d (was 188 in the 08-21 window — roughly doubled) and it is now CONTENT-crawling, not onboarding: 9 of the 10 /cycles/<slug> routes (all but modelski), all 8 paired data CSVs at 5 fetches each, the .md prose mirrors (about.md, methods.md, colophon.md), llms.txt, and the spectral SVGs. Google-family TOTAL fell 731 -> 447 only because the one-off GoogleOther onboarding sweep (543 -> 48) is over; the sustained-crawl number is the one that doubled. The llms.txt + .md-mirror + reuse-packet strategy is being consumed by Googlebot, not just LLM crawlers. (2) BING ARRIVED, UNPROMPTED AND AT PARITY. Bingbot 373 hits/14d, absent entirely from the 08-21 read. It crawled ALL 10 cycle routes plus /cycles (20), /methods (19), /poster (18), /about (18), /embed/docs (20), /state/2026 (13). No Bing Webmaster Tools property exists — this is organic discovery off robots.txt/sitemap. A second search engine is now a live channel and is UNMEASURED on the impressions side, exactly as Google was before 08-20. (3) THE LLM CHANNEL BROADENED — BUT THE PER-CRAWLER TOTALS ARE PARTLY SPOOFED, SO READ COVERAGE, NOT byWho. A single vulnerability scan on 2026-08-28 08:28-08:31Z made 643 requests while ROTATING crawler user-agents, and the classifier attributed them by UA: 68 'Meta/Facebook', 57 'OAI-SearchBot', 55 'GPTBot', 51 'Amazonbot', 27 'Applebot', 26 'PerplexityBot', 23 'Bytespider', 20 'Google-Extended', 19 'ClaudeBot', 295 'other bot'. That is 83% of Google-Extended's entire 14-day total, 62% of Bytespider's, 60% of Meta's, ~35% of Amazonbot/Applebot/PerplexityBot. Whatever claimed to be GPTBot while requesting /api-keys.json was not GPTBot. This does NOT touch the findings above: the snapshot's per-crawler COVERAGE map is keyed on real site paths and excludes the 404 probe paths, so route-level claims are sound while the byWho volume column is not. Judged by coverage, the genuinely content-crawling set is: Googlebot, Bingbot, OAI-SearchBot (every cycle route + every .source.md + all three /api/v1 endpoints), GPTBot, Amazonbot (40 distinct paths incl. all 10 cycle routes) and Applebot. Real but shallow: PerplexityBot (6 paths), Meta/Facebook (6 — but notably /llms.txt + all three .md mirrors), ClaudeBot (3). Effectively absent from content: Bytespider (/robots.txt only) and Google-Extended (ZERO real paths — its 24 hits are the spoof burst plus robots noise, which is why its coverage map is empty). So 'eight crawlers' is the wrong headline; SIX crawl the content and two of the eight are noise. (4) THE HUMAN-RESIDUAL QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED IN THE NEGATIVE, and the 08-15 CAUTION should be read as confirmed rather than open: the snapshot's own path list shows the 18,572 'browser-ish' + 3,395 'unknown (no UA)' lines are dominated by vulnerability scanning — /.env and ~40 variants of it, /wp-config.php, /secrets.json, /terraform.tfstate, /root/.aws/credentials, /serviceAccountKey.json. Do NOT report those buckets as readers. (Not an incident: static Next.js, none of those paths exist; this is internet background noise.) STILL OPEN and now the ONLY open leg: impressions, queries, ranking position, and index coverage — the human-facing half. That needs the GSC console read on David's account and cannot be derived from request logs at all. Bing Webmaster Tools is now a second, cheap instrument worth the same one-time verification David did for GSC on 08-20.

WHAT THE COST ACTUALLY IS, measured rather than assumed. The tag is NOT undefined: src/app/(app)/cycles/[id]/page.tsx:247-253 renders 'Confidence classification: <LABEL> — <gloss>.' on EVERY per-cycle page, and each index entry links to exactly that page. So the definition is one click away from the tag on the destination the entry already points at, and it is also still on the index itself, below. Journey-walk 2026-08-24 J8's finding was that the tags 'were defined nowhere on the site'; that is no longer the accurate description of this regression. What changed is ORDER on one page, not existence.

CORRECTED 2026-09-21 at P5. This paragraph read 'WHAT SHIPPED WITH THIS ROW. The index tag now carries title={confidenceGloss(...)}' and that was FALSE when written: the tooltip was tried and REVERTED the same day, inside 2026-09-20's P4, and yesterday's report says so. The repo agrees — `grep -rn "confidenceGloss" src/` returns the glossary prose (src/app/(app)/cycles/page.tsx:352-358) and the per-cycle page (src/app/(app)/cycles/[id]/page.tsx:253) and no title attribute anywhere, and src/app/(app)/cycles/page.tsx:238-249 carries the comment recording the revert and its two reasons (hover-only, so it does nothing for the phone reader this row is about; and the extra element splits that line in check-rendered-text's extraction, perturbing the page's text baseline). Found by the report subagent at P5 2026-09-21, reading the row against the code rather than trusting it. SO: NOTHING shipped with this row. The tag has no affordance of any kind, on any input, and the read below is about a bare tag beside '30Y · PEAK 1970'. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. items.title: This lane's docs/daily-config.md declares no primer:handoff record, so every morning's SessionStart banner reports the primer as having no first-action section
items.hypothesis: The primer's FIRST ACTION is authored by hand inside the hand:begin/hand:end banner, which a human or agent reading the file finds immediately. The machine path does not: gen-primer-first-action resolves the GOVERNING action from a `primer:handoff` JSON record in docs/daily-config.md, and this lane has never declared one, so firstActionDeclared is false and the SessionStart hook reports the primer as declaring none.
items.notes:
FOUND 2026-09-20 at the close, by running the generator rather than assuming the primer was fine. This is the defect I personally paid for at THIS MORNING'S cold start: the SessionStart banner read `docs/cold-starts/2026-09-20.md (today) exists but declares NO first-action section (no <!-- primer:first-action --> marker and no "first action" heading). Read the file before acting.` The primer DID carry a first action — numbered item 1 in its banner — so the cost was a moment of doubt rather than a lost action, but the banner is wrong on the only morning it matters and it will be wrong again tomorrow.

THE READ: `node C:/dev/skylark/skylark-site/scripts/gen-primer-first-action.mjs --target-date 2026-09-21 --json` returns `"firstActionDeclared": false` and `handoff: { usable: false, reason: "one primer:handoff JSON record is required" }`.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED AT THE CLOSE THAT FOUND IT. The record is not a one-line marker. `readGoverningHandoff` (gen-primer-first-action.mjs:1848) parses it with `declaredHandoff`, then requires an `evidencePath` pointing at a tracked JSON file of execution evidence, and hands both to `validateHandoff` with the target date, the cwd and the repo's tracked-file list — all in ../skylark-site/src/lib/cc-primer-first-action-blocks.mjs, which I did not read. A record written from a guessed schema would be DECLARED-but-invalid, which is a worse state than absent: the generator would then own the banner region (finalizeGoverningHandoff only rewrites the hand region when `validation.declared`) and could overwrite an authored first action with an UNVERIFIED stub. So this is a task with a real read in front of it, not a close-time edit.

SECOND-ORDER, worth knowing before anyone starts: the same run warns `⚠ SHADOW — emitted command cannot run as written: node C:/dev/skylark/skylark-site/scripts … does not resolve from the lane`, because this lane has no `scripts/sky.mjs` (dead-ref-ok: the absence of that file IS this finding, so no edit can make the path resolve) and the generator emits a DIRECTORY where a file should be. That is the generator's defect, not this lane's, but it means the generated foot's release commands are currently unrunnable here and should not be pasted into a primer as-is.



RE-SCOPED 2026-09-22 (P2), on the orchestrator's P1→P2 ruling (bus da93e347), from my own P1 proposal (bus 4aa0d17d). WHAT I READ: the SessionStart hook finds a first action by a `<!-- primer:first-action -->` marker or by the first ATX heading matching /first[\s-]+action/i (~/.claude/hooks/sessionstart-mt-date-and-primer.mjs header lines 43-60, FIRST_ACTION_TEXT_RE at :169), and prepends a complete hand:begin banner to what it injects (withGoverning, :311-338). knownPatterns.detail: Round 4 of the external fact-check found the Strauss-Howe rationale claiming '2020 is a trough' when cos(2p*65/84) is approximately +0.15 (rising arm); an internal sweep found the same class of error in Turchin's parenthetical. knownPatterns.title: This Next version's JSX compiler eats element-adjacent spaces in multi-line text nodes
knownPatterns.detail: Live-verified 2026-08-24: a JSX text node that spans multiple source lines loses its leading/trailing whitespace even when the space sits on the same line as an adjacent inline element or {expression} — 'the {year} reading' rendered as 'the 2026reading', 'estimation conventionally' as 'estimationconventionally', symmetric case included ('theamplitude_normalized'). Single-line text nodes are unaffected, which is why the bug is invisible in source review and survives lint/tsc. A 31-junction sweep (9 files, commit e0b8422) converted every affected space to an explicit {" "}; the writing rule is recorded in AGENTS.md. Verify new prose against RENDERED HTML, not the TSX.

knownPatterns.title: A Next.js bump changes the emitted CSS bytes without changing a single style
knownPatterns.detail: Measured on the 16.2.4 -> 16.3.5 bump (2026-09-17, commit 7dadae1). A rendered-output gate that hashes the emitted CSS file reads DIRTY across a Next version change even when nothing visual moves: the 14 @font-face rules carry `url(../media/<contenthash>-s[.p].<token>.woff2)`, and that trailing <token> is a per-BUILD identifier that the bundler regenerates. Everything that matters was identical — 743 rules both sides, 60,063 bytes both sides, and the <contenthash> prefix (the font's own bytes) unchanged. Normalize that token away before comparing, and mind the shape: three of the live tokens contained a dot (`0zgw-jeven.3w`), so a pattern using [^.)]+ for the token silently fails to match on one side and manufactures a difference. Independent confirmation that a normalized-clean read is a real clean read: the production frames re-captured after the deploy were BYTE-IDENTICAL to the ones committed before it. Do not read this class of diff as a reason to revert; do not skip the CSS leg either, because a real restyle looks nothing like this. 2026-09-18: the TEXT leg of that gate is now committed as scripts/check-rendered-text.mjs (e5c53c4) — snap before, diff after, over a URL, an .html file, a directory of them, or a saved snapshot. The CSS leg is deliberately NOT in it, for the reason this row exists; rebuild that part per the normalization above when a bump needs it.

knownPatterns.title: A panel's CACHED total reads as a live finding for a while after you fix the thing it counts
knownPatterns.detail: Measured 2026-09-17. `check-engineering-zero.mjs --project sinusoidal-cycles` reads this lane's Dependabot total from the /api/cc panel cache, not from GitHub. After a400821 closed 16 alerts, the gate still RED on exactly those 16 for ~40 minutes while `gh api repos/u00dxk2/sinusoidal-history/dependabot/alerts?state=open --paginate` — the authoritative read — already showed them gone. Read the two together before acting: the gate's own count came from a cache, so a remainder it names that matches the set you just closed is a stale total, not a second finding, and the fix is to wait for the cache rather than to waive or re-open anything. The discriminator is cheap and it is the API read, never a re-run of the gate. Same day, the same distinction held in the other direction: the 30 alerts the gate named that the API also named were real, and they took a framework bump to clear. Do not generalize this into distrust of the gate — it is right about everything it reads from the ledger, and its Dependabot leg is right as soon as the cache turns over.
